title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: section 3 of Grothendieck's c.1970-72 notes on crystalline Dieudonné theory. These parallel his ICM Nice 1970 talk and his Montréal 1970 lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné'. Section 1 treated abelian schemes A/S: the crystal D*(A) was built cohomologically, and also as Lie of the universal vector extension E(A*). The deformation theorem says that lifts of A to a nilpotent PD-thickening S' correspond to lifts of the Hodge filtration. Section 2 treats Barsotti-Tate (BT) groups. Section 3 compares the two theories. Assume p is locally nilpotent on S and use Berthelot's full crystalline site, not the nilpotent one. The key claimed result: for A/S variable, there is a functorial isomorphism compatible with base change, D*(A(∞)) ≅ R^1 f_{cris*} O_{A_cris}. Here A(∞) = A[p^∞] is the BT group of A, and the right side is the first relative crystalline cohomology crystal. Evaluated on S, this isomorphism matches the Dieudonné filtration with the Hodge filtration on H^1_dR(A/S). This uses t_{A(∞)} ≅ t_A and the analogous isomorphism for A*. A marginal note says this comparison is the heuristic origin of the definition of D*(G) for an arbitrary BT group G: one postulates the isomorphism and extracts a definition. Consequence: for a thickening S' → S with locally nilpotent divided powers, the deformation theory of A coincides with that of A(∞). By dévissage on the order of nilpotence one obtains the Serre-Tate theorem: deformations of A are the same as deformations of A[p^∞]. A marginal note says this is the method Messing followed in his thesis. A bracketed aside defines a universal vector extension E(G) of a BT group. It asserts a canonical isomorphism E(A(∞)) ≅ E(A)(∞), and from it, by the usual crystalline extension procedure, an isomorphism of crystals in groups. A deleted item 4 was to be 'passage à la limite'. A second deleted item 4 posed the problem of finding the functor from filtered F-crystals to p-adic sheaves, i.e. Grothendieck's 'mysterious functor'.
errors: No mathematical error. The comparison isomorphism and its filtration compatibility are stated, not proved; the proofs appeared later (Mazur-Messing 1974; Berthelot-Breen-Messing 1982).
The symbols for the two filtrations are left blank in the typescript ('compatible aux filtrations ___ et ___').

E(A)(∞) should be read as the p^∞-torsion colimit of E(A). Because p is locally nilpotent, the vector part is p-power torsion, so E(A)(∞) is an extension of A(∞) by the vector group. This is consistent, though not spelled out.

ideas.what: Isomorphism between the crystalline Dieudonné crystal of A[p^∞] and H^1_cris of A, compatible with Hodge/Dieudonné filtrations

deep.surprise_reason: Every idea here (crystalline comparison, Serre-Tate via deformation theory, universal extension of BT groups, the mysterious functor) is well known and properly credited to Grothendieck, Messing and Mazur-Messing. The only mildly interesting historical detail is the explicit admission that D*(G) was arrived at heuristically by postulating the comparison isomorphism.
